questions: Are you currently experiencing pain in your lower back?
Does the pain shoot or radiate down your leg, past the knee toward the foot?
Did this pain begin after lifting a heavy object or making a sudden movement?
Have you had a fever in the past few days?
Do you have numbness, tingling, or "pins-and-needles" in your leg or foot?
Have you noticed weakness in your foot or ankle, such as foot drop or difficulty walking on your toes/heels?
Have you had any loss of bowel or bladder control, or difficulty urinating?
Do you have a severe headache?
Have you had neck stiffness or pain when trying to bend your neck forward?
Have you had any previous back injuries, back surgery, or chronic back problems?
Is the pain worse when coughing, sneezing, or straining?
results: 1. speed of onset: chorea was the INITIAL manifestation of the stroke in 57% of the series; two patients within 24 hours, three between days 2 and 5
2. blood glucose: normal - non-ketotic hyperglycaemia was an exclusion criterion for this series
3. CT head (non-contrast): ischaemic stroke - 92.9% of the series were ischaemic and one was haemorrhagic
4. brain MRI with contrast: lesions in the LENTIFORM NUCLEUS (50%), insula (35.7%), caudate (14.3%) and thalamus (14.3%); cortical in 35.7%, deep in 35.7%, both in 28.6%
